bib.title: VOYAGER: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models

read.skipped: Appendix A prompt bodies (A.3.4-A.5) and skill-library code examples skimmed for structure, not read line by line; item lists in B.4.1 skimmed.

question: Can an LLM agent learn continually in an open-ended world, accumulating reusable skills without any parameter updates?
hypothesis: An automatic curriculum, a growing library of verified code skills and iterative prompting with feedback let a blackbox LLM agent explore and learn lifelong without fine-tuning.
contributions: Voyager, the first LLM-powered embodied lifelong learning agent in Minecraft
Automatic curriculum, skill library of executable code and iterative prompting with environment feedback, execution errors and self-verification
Gains over ReAct, Reflexion and AutoGPT in items, tech tree speed and distance, and zero-shot transfer

method.summary: GPT-4 acts through code in Minecraft (MineDojo plus Mineflayer). A curriculum prompt proposes tasks, GPT-4 writes code refined up to 4 rounds with environment feedback, execution errors and a GPT-4 critic, and verified programs are stored in an embedding-indexed skill library.
method.task: open-ended embodied lifelong learning in Minecraft

datasets.name: Minecraft (MineDojo simulation)
datasets.split: 3 trials per method; zero-shot tests in a newly instantiated world

other.uses: self-ask questions, skill descriptions, query suggestion

inference.temperature: 0 for all calls except automatic curriculum at 0.1
inference.samples: 3 trials per method; 160 prompting iterations (exploration and tech tree), 50 iterations (zero-shot)
inference.prompting: System plus user prompt concatenated per call; chain-of-thought; at most 4 code-generation rounds per task before the curriculum is asked for another task
inference.retrieval: Skill library as vector DB keyed by embedding of GPT-3.5 description; query is GPT-3.5 plan plus environment feedback; top-5 skills put in prompt

parameters.curriculum_warmup: info added as tasks completed (Table A.1: nearby entities after 5, full inventory 7, biome/blocks 10, health/hunger/time/context 15)

other.cost: GPT-4 is 15x more expensive than GPT-3.5

metrics.name: unique items
metrics.definition: distinct items obtained within 160 prompting iterations

metrics.name: tech tree milestone
metrics.definition: mean prompting iterations to unlock wooden/stone/iron/diamond tool, with successful trials out of 3

metrics.name: map coverage
metrics.definition: smallest circle enclosing the agent trajectory

metrics.name: zero-shot task completion
metrics.definition: iterations to solve unseen task in new world, max 50

eval.protocol: Three trials per method; no significance test; baselines re-interpreted for MineDojo with the task 'explore the world and get as many items as possible'.

prompts.text: You are a helpful assistant that tells me the next immediate task to do in Minecraft. My ultimate goal is to discover as many diverse things as possible, accomplish as many diverse tasks as possible and become the best Minecraft player in the world.
Your function will be reused for building more complex functions. Therefore, you should make it generic and reusable.

limits: Authors: GPT-4 API is costly (15x GPT-3.5) and GPT-3.5 or open-source LLMs cannot match its code quality
Authors: agent can get stuck; self-verification can miss success (spider string); curriculum and code hallucinate (copper sword, cobblestone fuel)
Only 3 trials per method, no variance tests; baselines are re-implementations adapted by the authors, not tuned originals
Uses high-level Mineflayer API, so no perception or motor control; text-only GPT-4 at time of writing
Model snapshots (gpt-4-0314) are deprecated; a gpt-4-0613 rerun is reported as similar

lineage.note: Voyager's self-verification is said to be more comprehensive than self-reflection
simulation environment and wiki knowledge base
Mineflayer low-level controller following this work

figures.caption: VOYAGER consists of three key components: an automatic curriculum for open-ended exploration, a skill library for increasingly complex behaviors, and an iterative prompting mechanism that uses code as action space.

figures.caption: Ablation studies for curriculum, skill library, GPT-4 and for the iterative prompting mechanism.
figures.why: Shows each component's contribution over iterations
